summary: Santa Maria is a smooth, medium-weight engine builder where you place tetromino-shaped buildings on your colony board and activate whole rows or columns with placed dice, chaining production in a satisfying cascade. It scales well solo to four players and rewards planning your colony's layout more than any direct fight with opponents.
praised: quick to teach relative to its depth
criticised: multiplayer solitaire feel with little direct interaction
can suffer analysis paralysis planning colony layout
some expansion content adds complexity creep

interaction.kind: drafting dice from a shared pool that others also want
interaction.detail: The only shared element is the common pool of dice each round — taking a die you need denies it to someone else, but that's the extent of the friction. The overwhelming majority of decisions (placing polyominoes, activating rows/columns) happen entirely on your own private colony board with no way to affect an opponent's.
interaction.said: the publisher's own description states the game 'has no direct destructive player conflict', and it's generally discussed as a relaxed, low-conflict euro built around your own colony board.

subsystems: colony building via polyomino placement and dice activation
scoring.how_you_win: Build and activate your colony efficiently across a fixed number of rounds, buying privilege cards and advancing your ship; the most accumulated VP at the end wins.
